move: full-frame kaleidoscope irises to a disc, slide text rises, bursts back
how: An offscreen 1400px tile of 220 seeded circles, triangles and bars drifts on sines; it is mirrored into 12 clipped wedges on a full-frame canvas and again, smaller, inside a 230px disc. A GSAP timeline spins the pattern two wedges per loop (ease none) and breathes zoom 1.2 to 0.85 with sine.inOut yoyo. At 0.3D the full canvas irises shut via clip-path circle(120%) to circle(0%) over 1.1s (expo.inOut); the disc scales in from 0 with rotation -90 (back.out(1.6)), and kicker, two title lines, a scaleX bar and a footer rise from yPercent 110 with expo.out staggers. At 0.84D everything leaves upward (expo.in) and the clip-path reopens over 0.5s (expo.out) so the loop restarts on the full kaleidoscope.
adapt: Swap the kicker/title/footer strings, the six shape colours, the tile background and the seed; keep the 12-segment mirror, the two-wedge spin per loop, and the 1.5s / 4.2s iris in/out beats.
port: mount(el, shot) builds both canvases and the .slide copy in el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with an extra {u:0->1, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate redraws the source tile and both kaleidoscopes from the st.spin/st.zoom values (the fx.register seek). Scope '#k', '.disc', '.kick', '.title', '.bar', '.foot' to el and give the canvases unique ids.
caveats: from() tweens on .kick/.title/.bar/.foot need immediateRender:false when ported
redraws a 1400px source and 24 clipped drawImage wedges every frame
the reopen ends at 5.05s, 0.05s past D, so the last frame is a hair short of the first
